summary:
[  edit  ]
The Movie File In  TOP  loads movies, still images, or a sequence of still images into TOPs. It will read images in  .jpg ,  .gif ,  .tif , or  .bmp  format. It will read movies in QuickTime's  .mov  format,  .mp4 ,  .mpg ,  .mpeg ,  .avi ,  .wmv ,  .dpx ,  Cineform  and  Hap  Q formats (including Hap Q with Alpha).
It also supports the  NotchLC  codec,  EXR  files ( .exr ) and some  .swf  and  .flv  Flash files as well as DXT1/3/5 and RG compressed  .dds  files. Images and movies can also be fetched from the web by using  http://  to specify a URL.
Access the hardware decoder on Nvidia GPUs with the Hardware Decode parameter on the 'Tune' page. This supports 10 and 12-bit H264/H265s and YUV 444 files on supporting hardware, converted into 16-bit pixel channels. Other codecs that this also decodes include VP8, VP9, JPEG, AV1, VC1.
More information  here.
When reading file formats that support higher bit depths such as 10-bit/16-bit/32-bit, an appropriate pixel format will be automatically used as long as the 'Pixel Format' menu on the Common page is left as 'Use Input'. i.e. a 16-bit file will cause each pixel to have 16-bits per color channel automatically.
For a complete list, see  File Types .
Examine the state of a Movie File In  TOP  by attaching an  Info CHOP  to it (see below on Info  CHOP ). This will show info like movie length, resolution, the number of images per second (the  sample_rate  channel), and whether there is audio in the file.  It also shows dynamic information like movie open status, current frame, readahead frames and queue size, dropped frame count, CPU decode time and  GPU  upload time.
Note that a movie's "images per second" (sample_rate) may be different than the timeline's frames per second. When referring to the movie's "index", it's in reference to the sequence of images in the movie file, not related to the global project frame rate.
See also the page on Movie File In  TOP  optimizations  Movie Playback , plus  Hap ,  Movie File Out TOP ,  Cineform  and  Video Stream In TOP .

parameters.label: File
parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The path and name of the image or movie file to load. Image and movie formats are those found in  File Types .  You can specify files on the internet using  http://  ...

parameters.label: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO
parameters.description: 8859-1" standalone="yes" ?>

parameters.label: Reload
parameters.name: reload
parameters.description: ⊞  - Change from 0 to 1 to force the image to reload, useful when the file changes or did not exist at first.

parameters.label: Reload  Pulse
parameters.name: reloadpulse
parameters.description: Instantly reloads the file.

parameters.label: Play Mode
parameters.name: playmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Specifies the method used to play the movie, there are 3 options.

parameters.label: Locked to  Timeline
parameters.name: locked
parameters.description: This mode locks the movie position to the timeline. Scrubbing or jumping in the timeline will change the movie position accordingly. The parameters Play, Reset, Speed, and Index are disabled in this mode since the timeline is directly tied to movie position.

parameters.label: Specify Index
parameters.name: specify
parameters.description: This mode allows the user to specify a particular position in the movie using the Index parameter below. Use this mode for random access to any location in the movie.

parameters.label: Sequential
parameters.name: sequential
parameters.description: This mode continually plays regardless of the timeline position (the Index parameter is disabled). Reset and Speed parameters below are enabled to allow some control.

parameters.label: Timecode  Object / CHOP / DAT
parameters.name: timecodeop
parameters.description: This mode allows the user to set the movie index by reference to a timecode in the form of either a  CHOP ,  DAT , or  Timecode Class  object.

parameters.label: Play
parameters.name: play
parameters.description: Movie plays when 1, movie stops when 0.

parameters.label: Speed
parameters.name: speed
parameters.description: This is a speed multiplier which only works when Play Mode is  Sequential . A value of 1 is the default playback speed. A value of 2 is double speed, 0.5 is half speed and so on. Negative values will play the movie backwards.

parameters.label: Cue
parameters.name: cue
parameters.description: ⊞  - Jumps to Cue Point when set to 1. Only available when Play Mode is Sequential.

parameters.label: Cue  Point
parameters.name: cuepoint
parameters.description: ⊞  - Set any index in the movie as a point to jump to.

parameters.label: Cue  Pulse
parameters.name: cuepulse
parameters.description: Instantly jumps to the Cue Point position in the movie.

parameters.label: Cue Behavior
parameters.name: cuebehavior
parameters.description: ⊞  - Customize the Cue parameter's behavior.

parameters.label: On Release, Repeat Cued  Frame
parameters.name: repeat
parameters.description: When releasing the Cue parameter, immediately play the next frame.

parameters.label: On Release, Play Next  Frame
parameters.name: play
parameters.description: When releasing the Cue parameter, first play the cued frame before continuing to play the next frame.

parameters.label: Index
parameters.name: index
parameters.description: ⊞  - This parameter explicitly sets the movie position when Play Mode is set to Specify Index. The units menu on the right lets you specify the index in the following units: Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage). For example, assume you have a movie that internally is 25 fps, and the timeline that is 60 fps. If you set Units to Index and the parameter value to 25, you get the image that is 1 second into the movie. If you set the Units to Frames and set the value to 60 you get the same image at 1 second into the movie. When this number is negative the index will cycle back through the movie.

parameters.label: Cue Point Unit
parameters.name: cuepointunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units for this parameter from Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage).

parameters.label: Loop Crossfade
parameters.name: loopcrossfade
parameters.description: ⊞  - Crossfades the beginning and end of the movie together to create a smooth transition when looping. If the movie uses Trim options, it will crossfade Trim Start with Trim End positions.

parameters.label: Step Size
parameters.name: stepsize
parameters.description: Sets how many frames to skip before displaying next frame. For example, a StepSize of 30 will display every 30th frame. This timing of movie playback does not change, so with a Step Size of 30 and a sample rate of 30, a new frame will be displayed every second.

parameters.label: Audio Loop
parameters.name: audioloop
parameters.description: ⊞  - This menu helps you determine how to treat the audio as the end of a movie approaches. This is needed because of all the cases of playing a movie, like when driving with an index, the  TOP  will not know if you intend to loop it or not.

parameters.label: Silence
parameters.name: silence
parameters.description: Audio will go silent when movie ends.

parameters.label: Fade
parameters.name: fade
parameters.description: Audio will fade out when movie ends.

parameters.label: Index Unit
parameters.name: indexunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units for this parameter from Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage).

parameters.label: Image Sequence Indexing
parameters.name: imageindexing
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how an image sequence is ordered.

parameters.label: Zero Based
parameters.name: zero
parameters.description: Index the sequence of images starting at 0, after sorting them alphanumerically.

parameters.label: Filename Based
parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Index the sequence of images using the numbers on the end of the filenames. I.e a file named flower400.tiff will be frame index 400, regardless of if there are other files in the directory before it.

parameters.label: Loop Crossfade Unit
parameters.name: loopcrossfadeunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units for this parameter from Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage).

parameters.label: Timecode  Object / CHOP / DAT
parameters.name: timecodeop
parameters.description: Set the movie index with a reference to a timecode. Should be a reference to either a  CHOP  with channels 'hour', 'second', 'minute', 'frame', a  DAT  with a timecode string in its first cell, or a  Timecode Class  object.

parameters.label: Interpolate Frames
parameters.name: interp
parameters.description: Interpolates between frames based based on exact time. For example, if the index (in frames) is 1.5, then frames 1 and 2 will be blended 50-50. If the index is 1.7 then 30% of frame 1 is blended with 70% of frame 2 and so on.

parameters.label: Deinterlace
parameters.name: deinterlace
parameters.description: ⊞  - For movies that are stored as fields, where each image is made of two images interleaved together. A 30-frame per second movie would contain 60 fields per second. For each image, the even scanlines of the first field are interleaved with the odd scanlines of the second field. The Movie File In  TOP  has several ways of dealing with this:

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Output the movie images unchanged.

parameters.label: Even
parameters.name: even
parameters.description: Take only the even scanlines of the file's images and create the odd scanlines by interpolating between the even scanlines. (For historic reasons, scanline 0 is at the top of the images for the purpose of the deinterlacing.)

parameters.label: Field Precedence
parameters.name: precedence
parameters.description: ⊞  - Where fields are extracted one field at a time, this will extract the Even field first by default, otehrwise it will extract the odd field first. The video industry has not standardized on one or the other.

parameters.label: Even
parameters.name: even
parameters.description: When the disk files are fragmented. The Movie File In  TOP  will read frames of the movie into memory before they are used, this can eliminate pops or stutters in playback that occur from fragmented files, other resources accessing the hard drive, or movie looping.

parameters.label: Bottom Half is Alpha (AAA)
parameters.name: bottomhalfalpha
parameters.description: If enabled, the image/movie will have it's height halved, and the R channel from the pixels on the bottom half will be treated as if they were the alpha channel for the top half. Useful for cases where the image format does not support alpha natively.

parameters.label: Pre-Multiply RGB by Alpha
parameters.name: premultrgbbyalpha
parameters.description: ⊞  - Premultiplies the image.

parameters.label: Input Color Space
parameters.name: inputcolorspace
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls what color space the input data will be treated as. It will be converted to the Working  Color Space  when uploaded to the  GPU .

parameters.label: Automatic
parameters.name: automatic
parameters.description: Automatically try to determine the input's color space based on color space metadata available from the input, if any. If no color space can be determined, it is assumed to be sRGB.

parameters.label: sRGB
parameters.name: srgb
parameters.description: sRGB  color space, with sRGB transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: sRGB - Linear
parameters.name: srgblinear
parameters.description: sRGB  color space, with linear transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Rec.601 (NTSC)
parameters.name: rec601ntsc
parameters.description: Rec.601  with NTSC primaries color space, with Rec.601 transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Rec.709
parameters.name: rec709
parameters.description: Rec.709  color space, with Rec.709 (same as Rec.2020) transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Rec.2020
parameters.name: rec2020
parameters.description: Rec.2020  color space, with Rec.2020 (same as Rec.709) transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Rec.2020 ST2084PQ
parameters.name: rec2020st2084pq
parameters.description: Rec.2020  color space, with  Perceptual Quantizer  transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Rec.2020 HLG
parameters.name: rec2020hlg
parameters.description: Rec.2020  color space, with  Hybrid Log Gamma  transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: DCI-P3
parameters.name: dcip3
parameters.description: DCI-P3  color space, with D65 white point and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: DCI-P3 (D60)
parameters.name: dcip3d60
parameters.description: DCI-P3 "D60 sim"  color space, with D60 white point, and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Display-P3 (D65)
parameters.name: displayp3d65
parameters.description: Display-P3  color space, with D65 white point, and sRGB gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Display-P3 (D65) - Linear
parameters.name: displayp3d65linear
parameters.description: Display-P3  color space, with D65 white point, and linear transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: ACES2065-1
parameters.name: aces2065
parameters.description: 1  -  ACES 2065-1  (also known as ACES AP0) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: ACEScg
parameters.name: acescg
parameters.description: ACEScg  (also known as ACES AP1) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: ACESproxy
parameters.name: acesproxy
parameters.description: ACESproxy  color space, which has a log transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Passthrough
parameters.name: passthrough
parameters.description: When selected, the color values will be used as-is in the operation, without any modification or attempt to convert them into the Working Color Space.

parameters.label: Rec.709
parameters.description: Gamma 2.4   rec709gamma24  -

parameters.label: Input  Reference  White
parameters.name: inputreferencewhite
parameters.description: ⊞  - When converting the input color values to the Working Color Space, this controls how they should be treated with respect to  Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same  Reference  White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the  Reference  White level (brightness) of the colors will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR  Reference  White of 120 nits, and the HDR  Reference  White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

parameters.label: Default For Color Space
parameters.name: default
parameters.description: Will use either the SDR or the HDR  Reference  White, based on the color space detected/selected.

parameters.label: Standard (SDR)
parameters.name: sdr
parameters.description: Will treat the Input Color Space as SDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.label: High (HDR)
parameters.name: hdr
parameters.description: Will treat the Input Color Space as HDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.label: Loading/Error Image
parameters.name: loadingerrorimage
parameters.description: ⊞  - When the file can not be loaded for some reason, select what to display instead.

parameters.label: Colored Bottom Right Square
parameters.name: coloredbottomright
parameters.description: Show a colored square in the bottom right. Red means failed to load, grey means still loading.

parameters.label: Zero
parameters.name: zero
parameters.description: Show a blank frame.

parameters.label: Trim
parameters.name: trim
parameters.description: Enables the parameters below to set trim in and out points.

parameters.label: Trim Start
parameters.name: tstart
parameters.description: ⊞  - Trim the starting point of the movie.

parameters.label: Trim Start Unit
parameters.name: tstartunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units for this parameter from Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage).

parameters.label: Trim End
parameters.name: tend
parameters.description: ⊞  - Trim the ending point of the movie.

parameters.label: Trim End Unit
parameters.name: tendunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units for this parameter from Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage).

parameters.label: Extend Left
parameters.name: textendleft
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how the Movie File In  TOP  handles movie positions that lie before the Trim Start position. For example, if Trim Start is set to 1, and the movie's current index is -10, the Extend Left menu determines how the movie position is calculated.

parameters.label: Hold
parameters.name: hold
parameters.description: Displays the first frame in the movie range (the frame specified by Trim Start) for any position before Trim Start.

parameters.label: Cycle
parameters.name: cycle
parameters.description: Loops the movie range continuously.

parameters.label: Mirror
parameters.name: mirror
parameters.description: Loops the movie range in a zig-zag pattern. For example, playing backwards from Trim Start the movie will index will climb towards Trim End, at which point is will decend down towards Trim Start again and continue to zig-zag (or mirror) the further the movie plays backwards.

parameters.label: Black
parameters.name: black
parameters.description: Displays black frame for any movie position before Trim Start.

parameters.label: Extend Right
parameters.name: textendright
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how the Movie File In  TOP  handles movie positions that lie after the Trim End position. For example, if Trim End is set to 20, and the movie's current index is 25, the Extend Right menu determines how the movie position is calculated.

parameters.label: Hold
parameters.name: hold
parameters.description: Displays the last frame in the movie range (the frame specified by Trim End) for any position after Trim End.

parameters.label: Cycle
parameters.name: cycle
parameters.description: Loops the movie range continuously.

parameters.label: Mirror
parameters.name: mirror
parameters.description: Loops the movie range in a zig-zag pattern. For example, playing forwards from Trim End the movie will index will start decending towards Trim Start, at which point is will start climbing towards Trim End and continue to zig-zag (or mirror) the further the movie plays.

parameters.label: Black
parameters.name: black
parameters.description: Displays black frame for any movie position after Trim End.

parameters.label: Override  Sample Rate
parameters.name: overridesample
parameters.description: Turn On to change the sample rate of the movie. When loading an image sequence, use these parameters to set the playback speed for the sequence.

parameters.label: Sample Rate
parameters.name: samplerate
parameters.description: Set the sample rate for playback when 'Override  Sample Rate ' above is On.

parameters.label: Pre-Read Frames
parameters.name: prereadframes
parameters.description: Sets how many video frames TouchDesigner reads ahead and stores in memory. The Movie File In  TOP  will read and decode frames of the movie into CPU memory before they are used, this can eliminate pops or stutters in playback that occur from some frames taking too long to decode, other resources accessing the hard drive, or movie looping. When reading a sequence of image, having more Pre Read Frames will allow multiple images to be decode at the same time. This allows playback of heavy file formats such as .exr in real-time, assuming the machine has enough CPU cores.

parameters.label: Frame Read Timeout
parameters.name: frametimeout
parameters.description: The time (in milliseconds) TouchDesigner will wait for a frame from the hard drive before giving up. If the Disk Read Timeout time is reached, that frame is simply skipped. This also works for network files that are downloaded via http://.

parameters.label: Frame Timeout Strategy
parameters.name: frametimeoutstrat
parameters.description: ⊞  - When on, if the Disk Read Timeout is reached TouchDesigner will use the latest available frame in place of the skipped frame.

parameters.label: Keep  Frame
parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Keep showing the same frame that is currently being output.

parameters.label: Best for Playback
parameters.name: playback
parameters.description: Try to pick the best frame for playback. This may be a newer frame that what is shown, but not quite the frame that is requested.

parameters.label: Best for Seeking
parameters.name: seeking
parameters.description: Try to show any frame, either before or after the target frame. Good for when seeking the movie via a shuttle widget in a UI.

parameters.label: Always Load Initial  Frame
parameters.name: alwaysloadinitial
parameters.description: If this parameter is turned on, then for the first loaded frame the Frame Read Timeout will be ignored, and it will always wait for the first frame to ensure the node always starts up with a valid image.

parameters.label: File Open Timeout
parameters.name: opentimeout
parameters.description: The time (in milliseconds) TouchDesigner will wait for a movie to open. If the Disk Open Timout is reached, the Movie File In  TOP  will stop waiting and make its image all black, with a grey square in the bottom right corner. If the file still isn't opened the next time the  TOP  cooks, it'll wait again, and do the same. It'll keep doing this until the file is opened, or the open fails.

parameters.label: Pre-Download HTTP Addresses
parameters.name: predownloadhttp
parameters.description: When On, the file will be fully downloaded before playing. When Off, the file will be streamed from its currently URL.

parameters.label: Update Image
parameters.name: updateimage
parameters.description: Image will not update when set to 0. Movie index will continue to move forward but the output image will not update. This is useful when you are using a Movie Audio  CHOP  to get audio from the movie, but you don't care about the video.

parameters.label: Max Decode CPUs
parameters.name: maxdecodecpus
parameters.description: Limit the maximum number of CPUs that will be used to decode certain video codecs that are capable of multi-CPU decoding, such as H264/H265 and Cineform.	Note that this does not affect multi-threaded decoding for image sequence playback, which is instead controlled by increasing the Pre-Read Frame parameter.

parameters.label: High Performance Read
parameters.name: highperfread
parameters.description: This option should be used when playing back files that require very high SSD read speeds such as high resolution (4K+) HAP Q files. It greatly improves read performance in those cases. It should not be used for low resolution or low data rate files such as 1080p H264 files.

parameters.label: High Performance Read Factor
parameters.name: highperfreadfactor
parameters.description: When doing high performance reads, this parameter controls the size of the read operations that are done on disk. Whatever the largest operation the codec asks to be done, this is multiplied by the read factor and all subsequent reads will read that much data instead. This can result in higher throughput depending on the drives. For example if a request is made to read 1MB and the factor is set to 3, then instead the operations will read 3MB from the disk and the extra 2MB read will be ready for the next frame and will likely already have the next 2 frames available in CPU RAM.

parameters.label: Hardware Decode
parameters.name: hwdecode
parameters.description: Controls if this node should use hardware decoding via the Nvidia hardware decoder chip. You can check if hardware decoding is being used using the Info  CHOP , 'hardware_decode' channel. This parameter does nothing for Hap and NotchLC codecs, which are always hardware decoded.

parameters.label: Output  Resolution
parameters.name: outputresolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - quickly change the resolution of the  TOP 's data.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's resolution

parameters.label: Eighth
parameters.name: eighth
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Quarter
parameters.name: quarter
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Half
parameters.name: half
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 2X
parameters.name: 2x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 4X
parameters.name: 4x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 8X
parameters.name: 8x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Fit  Resolution
parameters.name: fit
parameters.description: Grow or shrink the input resolution to fit this resolution, while keeping the aspect ratio the same.

parameters.label: Limit  Resolution
parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit the input resolution to be not larger than this resolution, while keeping the aspect ratio the same.

parameters.label: Custom  Resolution
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Directly control the width and height.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enabled only when the  Resolution  parameter is set to Custom  Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.name: resmult
parameters.description: Uses the Global  Resolution  Multiplier found in  Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global  Resolution  Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this  TOP  is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Uses the aspect of the image's defined resolution (ie 512x256 would be 2:1), whereby each pixel is square.

parameters.label: Custom Aspect
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Lets you explicitly define a custom aspect ratio in the Aspect parameter below.

parameters.label: Aspect
parameters.name: aspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Use when Output Aspect parameter is set to Custom Aspect.

parameters.label: Aspect Menu
parameters.name: armenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used aspect ratios.

parameters.label: Input Smoothness
parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the  TOP .

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Fill  Viewer
parameters.name: fillmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determine how the  TOP  image is displayed in the viewer.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the same Fill Viewer settings as it's input.

parameters.label: Fill
parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: Stretches the image to fit the edges of the viewer.

parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer horizontally.

parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer vertically.

parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.name: best
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so no part of image is cropped.

parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.name: outside
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so image fills viewer while constraining it's proportions. This often leads to part of image getting cropped by viewer.

parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.description: Displays the native resolution of the image in the viewer.

parameters.label: Viewer Smoothness
parameters.name: filtertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering in the viewers.

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail. When the input is 32-bit float format, only nearest filtering will be used (regardless of what is selected).

parameters.label: Passes
parameters.name: npasses
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the  TOP  the specified number of times. For every pass after the first it takes the result of the previous pass and replaces the node's first input with the result of the previous pass. One exception to this is the  GLSL TOP  when using compute shaders, where the input will continue to be the connected  TOP 's image.

parameters.label: Channel Mask
parameters.name: chanmask
parameters.description: Allows you to choose which channels (R, G, B, or A) the  TOP  will operate on. All channels are selected by default.

parameters.label: Pixel Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Format used to store data for each channel in the image (ie. R, G, B, and A). Refer to  Pixel Formats  for more information.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's pixel format.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel.

parameters.label: sRGB 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: srgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel and stores color in sRGB colorspace. Note that this does  not  apply an sRGB curve to the pixel values, it only stores them using an sRGB curve. This means more data is used for the darker values and less for the brighter values. When the values are read downstream they will be converted back to linear. For more information refer to  sRGB .

parameters.label: 16-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16float
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba32float
parameters.description: Uses 32-bits per color channel, 128-bits per pixels.

parameters.label: 10-bit RGB, 2-bit Alpha, fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgb10a2fixed
parameters.description: Uses 10-bits per color channel and 2-bits for alpha, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16fixed
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 11-bit float (RGB), Positive Values Only
parameters.name: rgba11float
parameters.description: A RGB floating point format that has 11 bits for the Red and Green channels, and 10-bits for the Blue  Channel , 32-bits total per pixel (therefore the same memory usage as 8-bit RGBA). The Alpha channel in this format will always be 1. Values can go above one, but can't be negative. ie. the range is [0, infinite).

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.name: mono8fixed
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.name: mono16fixed
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono)
parameters.name: mono16float
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono)
parameters.name: mono32float
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.name: rg8fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 8-bits per channel, 16-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.name: rg16fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (RG)
parameters.name: rg16float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (RG)
parameters.name: rg32float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 32-bits per channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (A)
parameters.name: a8fixed
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 8-bits per channel, 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (A)
parameters.name: a16fixed
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 16-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (A)
parameters.name: a16float
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 16-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (A)
parameters.name: a32float
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 32-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha8fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 8-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha16fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha16float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha32float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 32-bits per channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: index
parameters.description: The current frame index being shown. This is in the  FPS  of the movie file, not in timeline frames.

parameters.label: true_index
parameters.description: When the movie has a Trim applied to it, this will show the actually frame index within the movie being shown.

parameters.label: index_fraction
parameters.description: Normalized index value going from 0-1 from start to the end of the movie.

parameters.label: file_resx
parameters.description: The width of the movie in pixels.

parameters.label: file_resy
parameters.description: The height of the movie in pixels.

parameters.label: start
parameters.description: Unused currently.

parameters.label: length
parameters.description: The length of the movie, in movie frames.

parameters.label: sample_rate
parameters.description: The  FPS  of the movie.

parameters.label: last_index_uploaded
parameters.description: The last movie frame uploaded to the  GPU .

parameters.label: mv_has_audio
parameters.description: 1 if the movie has an audio track, 0 if not.

parameters.label: preloading
parameters.description: 1 if the movie is currently preloading via the preload() Python method.

parameters.label: odd_field
parameters.description: When deinterlacing using Bob (split), 1 means the odd field is being shown, 0 means the even field is being shown.

parameters.label: last_frame
parameters.description: 1 if the last frame of the movie is currently being shown, 0 if not. Note that if a frame is dropped the last frame may never get shown, if the movie is looping.

parameters.label: loop_frame
parameters.description: 1 if the movie has just looped.

parameters.label: pre_read_misses
parameters.description: Counts how many times the node wanted to show a frame, but that frame wasn't already ready in the Pre-Read Cache.

parameters.label: last_pre_read_miss_wait
parameters.description: The amount of time the node last waited for a pre_read_misses frame to be read, in milliseconds.

parameters.label: hard_drive_timeouts
parameters.description: The number of times the node gave up reading a frame due to it not reading fast enough. The amount of time it will wait is controlled by the 'Frame Read Timeout' parameter.

parameters.label: num_pre_read_frames
parameters.description: The number of frames that have been pre-read, decoded, and are ready to be shown.

parameters.label: first_index_to_read
parameters.description: The frame index of the first index in the Pre-Read cache.

parameters.label: last_frame_hd_read_time
parameters.description: The amount of time spent reading the last frame from the hard-drive, in milliseconds.

parameters.label: last_frame_decode_time
parameters.description: The amount of time spent decoding/decompression the last frame on the CPU, in milliseconds. This does not account for time spent decoding on the  GPU  for codecs such as NotchLC, or Hardware Decoded codecs.

parameters.label: open
parameters.description: 1 if the movie's file is open.

parameters.label: opening
parameters.description: 1 if the movie's file is in the process of opening, but not open yet.

parameters.label: open_failed
parameters.description: 1 if opening the movie failed.

parameters.label: fully_pre_read
parameters.description: 1 if the Pre-Read Cache of the movie is filled with already decoded frames.

parameters.label: true_length
parameters.description: The true length of the movie, ignoring any trimming.

parameters.label: hardware_yuv_to_rgb
parameters.description: 1 if the YUV format the movie was encoded in is being converted to RGB on the  GPU .

parameters.label: has_non_av_track
parameters.description: 1 if the movie file has a track that is not video or audio, such as a subtitle track.

parameters.label: pre_read_fails
parameters.description: The number of times pre-reading a frame failed.

parameters.label: disk_read_mbit_rate
parameters.description: The amount of data being read per second off of the hard drive, in mega-bits.

parameters.label: has_decode_errors
parameters.description: 1 if the file is suffering from decode errors.

parameters.label: num_decode_chunks
parameters.description: For Hap codecs, how many chunks the file was encoded as.

parameters.label: hardrware_decode
parameters.description: If the Hardware Decode parameter is on, this will be 1 if the  GPU  is able to hardware decode the movie's codec.

parameters.label: resx
parameters.description: Horizontal resolution of the  TOP  in pixels.

parameters.label: resy
parameters.description: Vertical resolution of the  TOP  in pixels.

parameters.label: aspectx
parameters.description: Horizontal aspect of the  TOP .

parameters.label: aspecty
parameters.description: Vertical aspect of the  TOP .

parameters.label: depth
parameters.description: Depth of 2D or 3D array if this  TOP  contains a 2D or 3D texture array.

parameters.label: gpu_memory_used
parameters.description: Total amount of texture memory used by this  TOP .

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: The Graphics Processing Unit. This is the high
parameters.description: speed, many-core processor of the graphics card/chip that takes geometry, images and data from the CPU and creates images and processed data.

parameters.label: To "pulse" a parameter is to send it a signal from (1) an  exported  CHOP channel or (2) a python command or (3) a mouse click that causes a new action to occur immediately. A pulse via python is via the  .pulse()  function on a pulse
parameters.description: type parameter, such as Reset parameter in a  Speed CHOP . A pulse from a CHOP is typically a 0 to 1 to 0 signal in an exported channel.

parameters.label: The sub
parameters.description: Family  of  Component  types that are used to define and render 3D scenes. A  Geometry Component  is an Object that contains the 3D shapes to render. A  Camera COMP  and  Light COMP  are other Object types. Separately, "Objects" also refers to Python objects.

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.

parameters.label: The term "Frame" is a measurement of time used (1) in the  Timeline , (2) as a time
parameters.description: unit in CHOPs, and (3) as a time unit in movie files that are read into  TOPs  and written out from TOPs. The frame rate is the frames per second ( FPS ).

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: The width and height of an image in pixels. Most TOPs, like the  Movie File In TOP  can set the image resolution. See  Aspect Ratio  for the width/height ratio of an image, taking into account non
parameters.description: square pixels.

parameters.label: The viewer of a node can be (1) the interior of a node (the  Node Viewer ), (2) a floating window (RMB
parameters.description: >View... on node), or (3) a  Pane  that graphically shows the results of an operator.

parameters.label: The
parameters.name: Frames
parameters.description: per-Second that TouchDesigner's  Timeline  runs at. Set with  project.cookRate .
